population_note_text: Books population (optional, cancelled and post-dated vouchers excluded); Contra excluded throughout. A loan ledger's interest journals are vouchers whose only other ledger lines are its configured interest ledger or ledgers (the client's list of loans) and any ledger the client configures as TDS payable; every other voucher touching the loan ledger is a taken (credit) or repaid (debit) transaction, never classified by ledger name -- except one that both credits and debits the loan ledger, which is listed as the books hold it, not divided into entries.

figures.definition_text: Entries on loan ledger (tag b9a9795c) whose other lines are expense ledgers only, besides any TDS: each is read as a loan taken or repaid, not as interest. Clause 31 lists it, asking whether it is the lender's charge (or its reversal), where the lender and the running balance, or its own amount, make it reportable; an entry whose reportability is not computed is listed as not computed instead, without that question.

Taken/repaid entries listed as not computed -- because the two walks of the principal balance disagree on their reportability, or a loan taken may be reportable if earlier repayments paid interest first (bridge#802), or because a voucher listed as both crediting and debiting their loan comes on or before their date and their own amount is less than the limit: in no reportable total and not in the flag count.

findings.title_text: Loan taken against Invented Walker (cash mode): not computed -- the principal balance this test walks went below zero before it, and the books do not show how to read the credits after that (possible s.269SS/269T)
limits_text: The principal balance this test walks on this loan ledger (principal only: interest credited and TDS journals are not walked) went below zero before this entry. That can be an overpayment the lender owes back, or earlier repayments that included interest: the books do not say which. So this test reads the principal credits after it two ways: from the opening as the books show it, netting them against that balance; or from an opening floored at nil, reading each as a fresh loan. This loan taken is not reportable under the first and reportable and flagged under s.269SS/269T under the second, so neither is chosen: it is in no reportable total and not in the s.269SS/269T flag count. Entries dated the same day are walked in voucher-id order, which the books do not record, so a balance below zero within a day may exist only in that order.

The questions this test asks on a computed entry (the lender's charge, a returned debit, a repeated narration, the mode read from the ledger group) are not asked on this record, though the figures counting such entries may cite it.
ask_client_text: How earlier repayments to this loan were applied (to principal or to interest), and whether each later credit was the lender returning an overpayment or a new loan, with the amounts.

findings.title_text: One lender on more than one loan ledger: the limits are tested per ledger, not per lender
limits_text: This lender is configured on 2 loan ledgers (tags 109bf849, 34ba9c75). Clause 31 reportability, the s.269SS/269T test and the s.194A threshold are tested here ledger by ledger, while the law looks at the lender as a whole: an entry or interest that crosses a limit only on the lender's aggregate is not listed. The CA determines.

Lenders are matched by the configured lender name only, compared without case or surrounding spaces: the same person configured under two different names is not caught, and two people under one name are grouped. The CA confirms the lender list.
ask_client_text: Which loan ledgers are with the same person.

findings.title_text: Loan entries booked against another loan's interest ledger, or a shared one: read as loans taken or repaid; whether they are interest is the CA's to determine
limits_text: 1 entry on this loan ledger booked against only an interest ledger configured for another loan or declared shared (tag 1ef1c100), besides any TDS lines: read as a loan taken or repaid, with clause 31(a)/(c) and the s.269SS/269T test applied as to any other entry.

If an entry is interest to this lender booked to the wrong interest ledger, it is not a loan taken or repaid: it would leave clause 31, and a s.269SS/269T flag on it would not apply. The books do not show which; the CA determines.
ask_client_text: For each entry named, whether it is interest to Invented Person or a loan taken or repaid.

findings.title_text: Interest to a non-exempt lender over the s.194A threshold, no TDS ledger evidence
limits_text: Whether the assessee must deduct under s.194A is not known (see the deductor-status question): listed until it is confirmed.

Books only: lender type ('nbfc') comes from the client's setup, not from a notification lookup; confirm the lender is not itself a body notified as exempt under s.194A(3)(iii) beyond the lender types the rules already exempt.

s.40(a)(ia) disallows 30% of the interest on TDS default; the second proviso removes this if the lender's Form 26A (Rule 31ACB) shows the interest was returned as income -- s.201(1A) interest still runs either way.

Credits to this loan from expense ledgers only are not in the interest above (they are shown net of any TDS on them; the interest is gross). If one is the lender's charge, it is interest (s.2(28A)) and belongs in it. Until its ledger is named among the loan's interest ledgers it is read as a loan taken, and clause 31 lists it where the lender and the running balance, or its own amount, make it reportable, or as not computed where that is not decided.
ask_client_text: Confirm whether TDS under s.194A was deducted on interest to Invented Charge Finance.
If not deducted, confirm whether Form 26A is available for this lender.
